metadata.name: E/M Level Assessment Test Suite
metadata.description: Example test cases for E/M level evaluation based on MDM complexity

test_cases.clinical_note:
SUBJECTIVE: 45-year-old male with sore throat x 3 days. No fever, cough, or difficulty swallowing. No sick contacts.

OBJECTIVE: Temp 98.6F, pharynx mildly erythematous, no exudates. Negative rapid strep test.

ASSESSMENT: Viral pharyngitis.

PLAN: Supportive care, salt water gargles, return if symptoms worsen.

SUBJECTIVE: 62-year-old female with new onset chest pain, worse with exertion. History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Father had MI at age 55.

OBJECTIVE: BP 145/92, HR 88. Heart sounds regular. EKG shows nonspecific ST changes.

ASSESSMENT: Chest pain, concerning for unstable angina.

PLAN: Troponin x 3, stress test ordered, aspirin started. Discussed symptoms requiring ER visit. Cardiology referral placed.

SUBJECTIVE: 55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes for annual follow-up. Reports good glucose control at home. No hypoglycemic episodes. Taking metformin 1000mg BID.

OBJECTIVE: Weight 195 lbs (stable). Foot exam: normal sensation, pulses intact. HbA1c 6.8% (reviewed from lab).

ASSESSMENT: Type 2 DM, well controlled.

PLAN: Continue current regimen. Recheck HbA1c in 6 months. Ophthalmology referral for annual eye exam.

SUBJECTIVE: 78-year-old male with CHF presents with increased dyspnea and leg swelling over 5 days. Has been compliant with medications but admits to high sodium diet recently. Also notes worsening fatigue.

OBJECTIVE: BP 162/95, HR 92, SpO2 91% RA. JVP elevated to 10cm. 2+ bilateral LE edema. Crackles at lung bases. Weight up 8 lbs from last visit. BNP 1800 (up from 400). CMP shows Cr 1.8 (baseline 1.2).

ASSESSMENT: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation with fluid overload and acute kidney injury.

PLAN: IV furosemide 80mg now and monitor. Daily weights. Strict I/O. Consider admission if no improvement in 2 hours. Discussed disease severity with patient and family.

SUBJECTIVE: 35-year-old female with recurrent migraine headaches. Has had 3 episodes this month despite taking sumatriptan. Reports aura before each episode. No new neurological symptoms.

OBJECTIVE: Neurological exam normal. No papilledema.

ASSESSMENT: Chronic migraine with aura, increased frequency.

PLAN: Start topiramate 25mg daily for prophylaxis. Continue sumatriptan PRN. Headache diary recommended. Return in 6 weeks to assess response.
